description:
LOCATION: crate-jmap-contacts-server/README.md:232-233

CURRENT TEXT:
    - No storage backend ships with this crate. The in-memory
      MemoryBackend in tests/ is a test harness only.

ACTUAL STATE (per crate-jmap-contacts-server/src/lib.rs:39-44):
    /// In-memory reference implementation of [`ContactsBackend`].
    ///
    /// Gated behind `feature = "memory"`. Not production. See [`memory`]
    /// for the full module documentation.
    #[cfg(feature = "memory")]
    pub mod memory;

The MemoryBackend lives at src/memory.rs and IS shipped — under the
`memory` cargo feature — to downstream consumers. The README claim "No
storage backend ships with this crate" is now incorrect, and the
follow-up "the in-memory MemoryBackend in tests/" misdirects readers
who go looking for it.

PROBLEM:
This is the README's Gotchas section — the section consumers read when
they have a question about what is shipped, what is supported, and
where to look. The stale content tells them:
1. False: no storage backend ships ← refuted by feature = "memory"
2. False: the backend lives in tests/ ← it lives in src/memory.rs
3. Implied: don't expect to use it ← it IS publicly usable behind the
   feature gate

The JMAP-hwdv.6 commit ed112ab ("feat(contacts-server): add
memory::MemoryBackend reference impl + sibling fixes") moved the
backend from tests/common/ to src/memory.rs and exposed it. The README
Gotchas paragraph was not updated as part of that move.

WHAT CALLERS CANNOT DEPEND ON:
- That README "Gotchas" content reflects the current shipped state.
- That advice in the Gotchas section is actionable.

RECOMMENDED:
Replace README.md:232-233 with:

    - The in-memory `memory::MemoryBackend` (gated behind `feature =
      "memory"`) is a reference implementation, not production. It is
      intended for downstream contributors to study, for integration
      tests, and for smoke tests / examples. See the module docs for
      the explicit non-production caveats (in-memory state, no
      persistence, simplified RFC 9610 edge cases).

P2 because the failure mode is "consumer reads docs, gets misdirected,
files a confused issue" rather than runtime breakage, but the README
is the primary discovery surface for consumers.
title: README §'Gotchas' says 'MemoryBackend in tests/' but it now lives at src/memory.rs behind a feature gate — stale post-JMAP-hwdv.6
